papers.title: Beyond Binary Labels: Diagnostic Evaluation of LLM Safety with Prompt-Level Rubrics
reasons: 🎯 temas: vuln & threats, LLM, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Current LLM safety benchmarks predominantly rely on binary safe or unsafe labels, lacking explanatory depth and suffering from low consistency across automated judges. To address this, we introduce DiagSafe, a diagnostic evaluation framework that moves beyond binary classification by employing prompt-level rubrics. Grounded in globally applicable AI safety policies, each rubric provides explicit criteria along two dimensions: safety, which targets concrete harms with specific exemptions to suppress false positives, and usefulness, which independently evaluates instruction fulfillment. To ensure a robust and realistic evaluation, we construct a bilingual (English-Chinese) benchmark grounded in a comprehensive 84-label safety taxonomy, consisting of two subsets: DiagBase, which covers single- and multi-turn prompts with direct harmful queries and template-based jailbreaks, and DiagAttack, which embeds harmful intents into complex instruction-following tasks to form challenging instruction attacks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DiagSafe significantly enhances the reliability of LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, achieving 95.34% agreement with human annotations -- substantially higher than the 69%-87% achieved by the baselines -- and high inter-judge consistency (Cohen's $κ$ = 0.864). Furthermore, applying our framework reveals that leading LLMs differ markedly in their unsafe rates, and each model also exhibits unique vulnerabilities along different dimensions. In addition, we observe that models are particularly susceptible in Chinese and multi-turn contexts. Ultimately, DiagSafe provides a reliable and explainable tool for auditing and optimizing LLM alignment.

summary_es.tldr: Evalúa la seguridad de los LLM con rúbricas detalladas, superando las limitaciones de las etiquetas binarias y mejorando la fiabilidad.
summary_es.problema: Los benchmarks actuales de seguridad de LLM usan etiquetas binarias (seguro/inseguro) que carecen de profundidad explicativa y tienen baja consistencia entre evaluadores automáticos.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce DiagSafe, un marco de evaluación diagnóstica que utiliza rúbricas a nivel de prompt con criterios explícitos para seguridad (incluyendo exenciones) y utilidad, evaluadas independientemente.
summary_es.resultados: DiagSafe logra un 95.34% de acuerdo con anotaciones humanas (superando el 69-87% de los métodos base) y alta consistencia entre jueces (Cohen's κ = 0.864). Revela diferencias notables en tasas de inseguridad entre LLMs líderes y vulnerabilidades únicas por modelo. Los modelos son más susceptibles en chino y en contextos de múltiples turnos.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Proporciona una herramienta fiable y explicable para auditar y optimizar la alineación de los LLM, permitiendo una comprensión más profunda de sus fallos de seguridad más allá de una simple clasificación binaria.

papers.title: Correlated Failures of AI Approval Monitors
reasons: 🎯 temas: AI agents, fintech & payments, fraud detection
papers.abstract_en: Before an AI agent takes a consequential action, such as paying, messaging or changing code, several monitors check it. Their verdicts are combined by aggregating scores or by counting approvals, whatever inputs the monitors share. Monitors that share a base model or a poisoned input, however, may fail together. We borrow the fail-prone systems of distributed computing: lists of monitor sets that may fail together. A rule is safe if it executes no bad action and live if it blocks no good one. We measured twelve small open-weights monitors on payment approval under two pre-registered protocols. Without pre-registration, we also measured three closed frontier models (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon) and the open DeepSeek-V3.2. Every reliable fooling of a monitor into approving a fraud came through an evidence source and reached only that source's readers. Fooling it into blocking a correct payment depended on injection resistance, a monitor's refusal to follow instructions planted in its data. Small models and DeepSeek obeyed such notes. The three closed models ignored them in all but one case, and Opus also resisted persuasion tailored to it. On new data, a rule that counts sources instead of votes blocked 0.9% of correct payments, against 7.4% for the best counting rule, at equal safety. The pre-registered worst-case test failed. One attack left the approvers on a single source, so no rule over the twelve language-model monitors survives every measured attack. Adding a rule engine, which cannot be persuaded, restored the condition for a safe and live rule on the measured attacks. Diversify the inputs, harden the monitors, count sources, not votes.

summary_es.tldr: Los monitores de IA que aprueban acciones pueden fallar juntos; diversificar y contar fuentes, no votos, mejora la seguridad.
summary_es.problema: Los sistemas de IA que toman decisiones críticas dependen de múltiples monitores, pero estos pueden fallar simultáneamente si comparten fuentes de datos o modelos base, comprometiendo la seguridad y fiabilidad.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone aplicar conceptos de sistemas distribuidos (listas de conjuntos de monitores propensos a fallos) y diversificar las fuentes de entrada. Se compara contar fuentes en lugar de votos, y se evalúa la resistencia a la persuasión y la inyección de instrucciones maliciosas.
summary_es.resultados: Contar fuentes bloqueó el 0.9% de pagos correctos frente al 7.4% de las reglas de conteo de votos, con igual seguridad. Los modelos pequeños y DeepSeek-V3.2 fueron susceptibles a la persuasión, mientras que los modelos cerrados (Opus, GPT-6, Gemini 4) resistieron en su mayoría. Un ataque dejó a los aprobadores en una sola fuente, invalidando reglas basadas en doce monitores. Un motor de reglas externo restauró la seguridad y la viabilidad.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Mejorar la fiabilidad y seguridad de los sistemas de IA que toman decisiones críticas es esencial para su adopción práctica, previniendo fraudes y garantizando que las acciones legítimas no se bloqueen indebidamente.

papers.title: Prompt Injection Through Forensic Evidence: A Taxonomy and Proof of Concept of Anti-Forensic Attacks on LLM-Assisted Digital Investigations
reasons: 🎯 temas: LLM, AI agents, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are entering digital forensics as examination assistants and autonomous agents. Digital forensics inverts the usual setting for indirect prompt injection: the evidence under analysis is attacker-controlled by definition, and the examiner is obliged to read it closely. This makes the reasoning layer a new anti-forensic target, next to the classical ones of data and tools. Classical anti-forensic taxonomies do not cover it, and prompt injection defences do not anticipate it. We extend the anti-forensic model to reflect the manipulation of reasoning, and present a taxonomy of attacks carried through adversarial evidence: an attacker selects an objective, a technique, a payload location, and a concealment method. We observe a perception gap, i.e., the fact that deterministic tools, the human examiner, and the model perceive the same evidence differently, which is what lets an injection reach the model unseen by the examiner. We demonstrate three attacks against an LLM-assisted analysis pipeline, changing a reported conclusion, writing attacker-chosen content to the analyst's workstation, and causing outbound network traffic, each driven only by text planted on the seized device. Mitigations to these attacks are also proposed.

summary_es.tldr: Nuevos ataques de inyección de prompts explotan la evidencia digital para engañar a los asistentes de IA en investigaciones forenses.
summary_es.problema: Los modelos de lenguaje (LLMs) se usan en investigaciones forenses, pero la evidencia bajo análisis, controlada por el atacante, puede usarse para inyectar prompts maliciosos y manipular el razonamiento del LLM, un vector de ataque no cubierto por defensas actuales.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone una taxonomía de ataques de anti-forense que manipulan el razonamiento de los LLMs a través de evidencia adversarial. Se demuestra un 'gap de percepción' donde herramientas deterministas, el examinador humano y el LLM interpretan la evidencia de forma distinta, permitiendo ataques ocultos.
summary_es.resultados: Se demostraron tres ataques exitosos contra un pipeline de análisis asistido por LLM: cambio de conclusiones, escritura de contenido en la estación del analista y generación de tráfico de red saliente, todo mediante texto plantado en el dispositivo incautado. El resumen no especifica métricas numéricas de éxito.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Abre una nueva categoría de amenazas en ciberseguridad y forense digital, requiriendo nuevas defensas para proteger la integridad de las investigaciones asistidas por IA y la seguridad de los analistas.

papers.title: Where AI Vulnerability Discovery Harnesses Go Quiet: Structural False Negatives and Hidden Vulnerabilities
reasons: 🎯 temas: vuln & threats, LLM, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based vulnerability discovery harnesses can miss real, reachable vulnerabilities because of how the harness around the model is built. Steps that select code, filter it, and store and merge findings can drop a vulnerability before or after the model runs, independently of the model's capability, and the report usually gives no sign that this happened. These drops come from engineering choices, and errors. They leave vulnerabilities undetected, and an attacker who knows the harness's rules can also use them to hide a vulnerability on purpose. Understanding these drops shows how to build harnesses that fix or disclose them and are harder to evade. Starting from the two harnesses we maintain, Knostic's OpenAnt and raptor, and then examining 10 additional open-source harnesses, we mapped 13 points where such drops occur and organized them into a taxonomy. Using each harness's own code, we show a single file that six harnesses dropped before their model saw its code, five of them without notice. We propose engineering failure patterns mapped to these drops, and relate them to Ptacek and Newsham's work on intrusion detection evasion. The paper also covers content-steered verdicts and prompt injection, and gives design principles and tests for harnesses that report accurately what they analyzed. The reliability findings likely apply to other LLM harnesses, beyond vulnerability research and application security, and the evasion findings apply wherever an attacker can write or influence the code being checked. We also argue that harnesses built to be descriptive can, in effect, be prescriptive. Rules written to describe typical code and typical model replies end up deciding what is analyzed, and anything that does not conform is treated as absent or as "no vulnerability."

summary_es.tldr: Las herramientas de IA para encontrar vulnerabilidades en código pueden fallar silenciosamente, ocultando fallos reales y permitiendo ataques dirigidos.
summary_es.problema: Las herramientas de descubrimiento de vulnerabilidades basadas en LLMs (modelos de lenguaje grandes) fallan en detectar fallos reales y alcanzables debido a cómo se construyen los 'harnesses' (sistemas de soporte) que rodean al modelo. Estos sistemas pueden descartar vulnerabilidades durante la selección, filtrado, almacenamiento o fusión de hallazgos, sin dejar rastro.
summary_es.propuesta: El paper propone identificar y categorizar los puntos de fallo en los harnesses de IA para el descubrimiento de vulnerabilidades. Analiza 13 puntos de caída en 12 harnesses de código abierto, propone patrones de fallo de ingeniería y ofrece principios de diseño para crear harnesses más fiables y resistentes a la evasión.
summary_es.resultados: Se identificaron 13 puntos donde los harnesses pueden descartar vulnerabilidades. Se demostró que seis harnesses analizaron un archivo sin detectar un fallo que contenía, cinco de ellos sin advertencia. Los hallazgos de fiabilidad son aplicables a otros harnesses de LLM y los de evasión a escenarios donde un atacante puede influir en el código.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite construir herramientas de IA más robustas y fiables para la ciberseguridad, evitando que vulnerabilidades críticas pasen desapercibidas y dificultando que los atacantes oculten fallos intencionadamente. Mejora la seguridad del software al hacer el análisis más preciso.

papers.title: Did the Problem Actually Get Harder? Testing LLMs on Paired P and NP-Complete Problems Hardened by Adversarial Multi-Agent Rewriting
reasons: 🎯 temas: LLM, AI agents, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Many NP-complete (NPC) problems have a polynomial-time (P) twin that differs in a single structural detail, such as 3- versus 2-colouring a graph. A model that reasons rather than recalls should notice which side of this boundary a problem falls on, yet existing benchmarks either fix the wording of each task or ignore its complexity class, so they cannot separate the two. We introduce P2NPCBench, a benchmark of 12 problem families in which every NPC problem is paired with a P twin posed over the same surface. To remove the textbook cues that enable recall, we build it with AgentGAN, an adversarial multi-agent framework in which a generator rewrites each statement until a panel of frozen code models fails, while an executable validity gate keeps every rewrite answer- and class-preserving. The result is 2,114 hardened statements with hand-verified reference human solvers. Evaluating 12 proprietary and open-source models, we find that every model scores lower on NPC statements than on their P twins (35.4% vs. 63.8% pass@1), and that 95.1% of model-family pairs fail more often on the NPC side. A tenfold time limit raises NPC accuracy only from 28.5% to 31.9%, so failures stem from wrong or crashing programs rather than slow ones. Hardening also narrows the class gap from 24.8 to 14.6 points, showing that part of the apparent gap reflects familiarity with textbook phrasing rather than complexity class.

summary_es.tldr: Nuevos problemas de IA revelan que los LLMs fallan más en tareas complejas (NP-Completas) que en sus versiones fáciles (P), incluso con redacción similar.
summary_es.problema: Los modelos de lenguaje actuales (LLMs) no demuestran una comprensión profunda de la complejidad computacional, ya que no distinguen entre problemas fáciles (P) y difíciles (NP-Completos) cuando se presentan con redacciones similares.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce P2NPCBench, un nuevo benchmark que empareja problemas NP-Completos con sus 'gemelos' P, utilizando AgentGAN para reescribir las declaraciones de forma adversaria y eliminar pistas de recuerdo, asegurando que las soluciones sigan siendo correctas.
summary_es.resultados: Los LLMs obtienen una tasa de acierto del 35.4% en problemas NP-Completos frente al 63.8% en sus contrapartes P. El 95.1% de los modelos fallan más en la versión NP-Completa. Aumentar el tiempo de ejecución no mejora significativamente la precisión en los problemas NP-Completos.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Demuestra las limitaciones actuales de los LLMs en razonamiento complejo y la necesidad de benchmarks más robustos para evaluar su verdadera capacidad de resolver problemas, no solo de memorizar soluciones.

papers.title: A Unified Evaluation Framework of Physical Adversarial Robustness in the Edge VLM Era
papers.abstract_en: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable end-to-end visual grounding via language prompts and generative decoding, demonstrating largely improved zero-shot and open-vocabulary detection capabilities. As a result, VLMs are rapidly being deployed at the edge in safety-critical real-world systems. However, the physical adversarial robustness of edge VLMs has not been systematically studied, and the fundamental differences in output with modern object detectors create methodological challenges for fair evaluation. To compare the two families directly, we evaluate every selected representative model on one outcome: whether an adversarial patch worn on a person evades detection of the model. We report this by introducing a unified metric, conditional attack success rate (cASR), counted only on images the model still localizes under a matched gray occluder, and partition every failure into omission (no box), substitution (a box on the patch), and displacement (a box on neither). We benchmark the physical adversarial vulnerability of compact grounding VLMs against a range of object detectors, and find that the VLMs can be as vulnerable as the detectors. We disclose that failure mode is largely associated with the output format of a model rather than its architecture family. Of the three, only omission is visible to a downstream system; displacement and substitution return confident, well-formed boxes, making them potentially more dangerous failures. Further, we find that, under distribution shift, VLMs that primarily failed by omission instead shift to failing more by displacement/substitution. Thus, a grounding VLM can inherit the detector's vulnerability while showing the possibility to adopt more dangerous failure modes. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/ericliang1/physical-adversarial-robustness.

summary_es.tldr: Evaluamos la robustez física de los modelos de lenguaje visual (VLMs) en el borde, revelando vulnerabilidades y modos de fallo peligrosos.
summary_es.problema: La robustez física de los VLMs desplegados en el borde no ha sido estudiada sistemáticamente, y las diferencias en sus salidas dificultan la evaluación comparativa con detectores de objetos tradicionales.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce un marco de evaluación unificado con una métrica (cASR) que mide el éxito del ataque de parches físicos, clasificando los fallos en omisión, sustitución y desplazamiento, y se evalúan VLMs compactos frente a detectores de objetos.
summary_es.resultados: Los VLMs pueden ser tan vulnerables como los detectores de objetos. El modo de fallo (omisión, sustitución, desplazamiento) está asociado al formato de salida, no a la arquitectura. Los fallos de desplazamiento y sustitución son más peligrosos ya que devuelven cajas bien formadas. Bajo cambios de distribución, los VLMs que fallan por omisión migran a fallos por desplazamiento/sustitución.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Los VLMs en el borde, usados en sistemas críticos, pueden heredar vulnerabilidades de los detectores y presentar modos de fallo más sigilosos y peligrosos, requiriendo nuevas estrategias de defensa.

papers.title: Compaction Laundering: Provenance Destruction in Context-Compacting Coding Agents
papers.abstract_en: Coding agents that run long enough must compact their context, summarizing the conversation, discarding the original, and carrying the summary forward as memory. We show that in popular open-source coding agents this step is an exploitable trust boundary. Harnesses that flatten the typed conversation into a single plain string, marking each message with a text label such as [User]:, destroy message provenance in code, before the summarizer runs. An attacker who controls anything the agent reads can forge a user turn that survives compaction as a genuine instruction. Across five flattening harnesses (pi, opencode, Cline, Aider, OpenHands) the forged approval launders into the agent's memory 87-100% of the time, up to a ~908,000-token context window; across four role-typed harnesses (Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Continue) the identical attack succeeds 0% of the time. We follow the attack to executed consequences. A laundered standing approval drives real tool-running agents to execute attacker-controlled curl | sh in a sandbox, and end to end in the live pi TUI at ~50% against a 0% paired clean arm. The same channel reliably steers an agent's plan away from a file an attacker designates off-limits, which can blind a code review to a planted backdoor. Because the provenance is destroyed deterministically in harness code, no prompt-level defense can restore it; we measure a code-level provenance check that catches 77% of laundering while demoting 2% of legitimate summary content. The defect also has a straightforward fix at the serializer, escaping the role labels before flattening; the role-typed harnesses avoid it entirely by keeping messages role-typed.

summary_es.tldr: Agentes de IA que resumen conversaciones destruyen el rastro de los mensajes, permitiendo a atacantes inyectar comandos maliciosos.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes de IA que compaginan su contexto para ahorrar memoria descartan la información original, creando una vulnerabilidad donde un atacante puede fabricar instrucciones que sobreviven al resumen y se ejecutan como legítimas.
summary_es.propuesta: Se demuestra que los 'harnesses' (mecanismos de ejecución) que aplanan la conversación en una sola cadena de texto destruyen la procedencia de los mensajes antes de que el resumen ocurra. Se propone una solución a nivel de código que escapa las etiquetas de rol antes de aplanar.
summary_es.resultados: El ataque de falsificación de aprobación sobrevive a la compactación el 87-100% de las veces en cinco 'harnesses' de aplanamiento. En agentes reales, el ataque ejecutó comandos como `curl | sh` en un sandbox con un 50% de éxito. Una verificación de procedencia a nivel de código detecta el 77% de los ataques.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Esta vulnerabilidad permite a atacantes secuestrar agentes de IA para ejecutar código arbitrario o manipular su comportamiento, incluso evadiendo revisiones de código. La solución a nivel de código es crucial para la seguridad de los sistemas de IA.

papers.title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
papers.abstract_en: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment. While external memory systems attempt to bridge this gap, they mostly act as passive retrieval caches, evaluated primarily by whether they can recall stored facts or past interactions. Whether memory can drive genuine continual learning remains an open question. In this paper, we introduce Memory-Centric Continual Learning (MCCL), arguing that memory should be judged by whether it improves future actions, not merely what it retrieves. MCCL has three main parts. First, a three-axis taxonomy organizes memory by where state is stored (substrates), what form it takes (assets), and how it is managed (policies). This defines a two-loop lifecycle that updates memory state in an inner loop while refining management policies in an outer loop based on task feedback. Second, an evaluation protocol measures retention under interference, adaptation to change, and task transfer to isolate genuine behavioral gains from simple context expansion. Third, a memory scaling framework models how agent performance scales with experience, storage capacity, and compute budgets across non-parametric and parametric memory. Together, these components reframe agent memory from passive lookup to continuous learning, offering a principled route toward self-improving autonomous agents.

summary_es.tldr: Aprendizaje continuo para agentes de IA: una nueva perspectiva centrada en la memoria para la mejora continua.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes de IA actuales con modelos fundacionales tienen limitaciones en el aprendizaje continuo debido a pesos fijos y límites de contexto, y los sistemas de memoria externos actúan principalmente como cachés pasivos de recuperación.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce el Aprendizaje Continuo Centrado en la Memoria (MCCL), que trata la memoria como un motor para el aprendizaje continuo en lugar de una simple recuperación. MCCL utiliza una taxonomía de memoria, un protocolo de evaluación y un marco de escalado para mejorar las políticas de gestión de memoria y el rendimiento del agente.
summary_es.resultados: El resumen no especifica resultados numéricos concretos, pero propone un marco para evaluar la retención, adaptación y transferencia de tareas, y modelar la escalabilidad del rendimiento con la experiencia y los recursos.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite el desarrollo de agentes de IA autónomos capaces de aprender y mejorar de forma continua y sostenible a lo largo del tiempo, superando las limitaciones actuales de los modelos fijos y la memoria pasiva.

papers.title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
papers.abstract_en: Using an LLM to generate training data for another is among the most general ways to train one, and it remains common practice. Some frontier teams have closed that route for their own models: what comes back is an answer, or a short summary, without the detailed reasoning trace behind it. That is a little ironic: they were themselves built on distilling human knowledge, and distilling an open-source model is still entirely routine; the restriction applies to their own outputs alone. Recent work recovers the hidden reasoning by replaying encrypted blocks across models. It somehow works, but it breaks the providers' terms of service, so it is not something a product can be built on long-term. We built the alternative. We take the context and the teacher's answer as input, and generate the reasoning trace ourselves, in the style of the student's own model family. Training is two-stage, supervised and then adversarial: a generator learns to regenerate the family's own reasoning traces from their context and answer, and a critic learns how real a reasoning trace looks. Applied to a teacher's answer, the generator writes one in the family's style. An independent judge rates how likely traces are to be genuine on a scale from 0 to 1: ours average 0.68, real traces 0.66, and traces selected by the critic from four candidates 0.82. These are authenticity scores, not correctness rates. We test the idea on five benchmarks with everything else held fixed. On general tasks the five training corpora are about the same; on coding, the generated reasoning beats Fable 5's own thinking content. With the same 5,000 questions and the same teacher answers, HumanEval+ improves by 3.7 points and MBPP+ by 7.1 at the final checkpoint, and the MBPP+ lead holds at every checkpoint. We suspect that reasoning written in the student's family style is easier for it to learn from.

summary_es.tldr: TraceForge genera razonamientos de IA al estilo del modelo estudiante, mejorando el aprendizaje y la autenticidad de los datos de entrenamiento.
summary_es.problema: Los modelos de IA de vanguardia restringen la generación de datos de entrenamiento detallados, limitando la capacidad de otros modelos para aprender de su razonamiento. Métodos anteriores para recuperar este razonamiento violan los términos de servicio.
summary_es.propuesta: TraceForge genera trazas de razonamiento al estilo de la familia del modelo estudiante, utilizando el contexto y la respuesta del modelo 'profesor'. El entrenamiento es en dos etapas: supervisada (generador aprende a replicar trazas) y adversarial (crítico evalúa la autenticidad de las trazas).
summary_es.resultados: Las trazas generadas por TraceForge obtienen una puntuación de autenticidad promedio de 0.68 (frente a 0.66 para trazas reales). En benchmarks de codificación, mejora HumanEval+ en 3.7 puntos y MBPP+ en 7.1 puntos en comparación con el razonamiento propio de Fable 5.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite a los modelos de IA aprender de razonamientos auténticos y estilísticamente consistentes, superando las restricciones de los modelos de vanguardia y mejorando el rendimiento en tareas específicas, especialmente en codificación.

papers.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Compositionality
papers.abstract_en: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge. Modern pipelines combine embedding, chunking, retrieval, reranking, query augmentation, context compression, and agentic verification, yet these techniques are typically evaluated one at a time. It remains unclear whether their isolated gains survive composition, whether retrieval quality and answer faithfulness favor the same design choices, and whether conclusions from small corpora hold at large scale. We pre-declare three hypotheses and introduce LASAGNA, an open-source framework for controlled RAG evaluation. We test 450 configurations across eight benchmarks and corpora ranging from 5K to 200K documents. Three findings emerge. First, individually strong techniques from different phases of a RAG pipeline do not necessarily compose: three retrieval techniques predict a +47% combined improvement but deliver only +17% when used together. Second, component gains stack differently for retrieval and faithfulness, and optimizing one can hurt the other. Third, the best composition changes as the corpus grows: the combination that wins on a small corpus may not remain best at large scale. These findings show that gains measured in isolation are not reliable predictors of realistic performance, and that new RAG techniques should be tested with the full surrounding stack. We call on researchers to do so and supply LASAGNA to simplify these experiments.

summary_es.tldr: Evaluar la composición de técnicas de Generación Aumentada por Recuperación (RAG) revela que las mejoras individuales no siempre se suman, afectando la calidad y fidelidad.
summary_es.problema: Las técnicas de RAG se evalúan de forma aislada, sin saber si sus mejoras individuales se mantienen al combinarlas, si optimizar la recuperación afecta la fidelidad de la respuesta, o si los resultados a pequeña escala se mantienen en corpus grandes.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce LASAGNA, un framework de código abierto para evaluar RAG de forma controlada, probando 450 configuraciones en 8 benchmarks y corpus de hasta 200K documentos, y se plantean tres hipótesis pre-declaradas.
summary_es.resultados: Las técnicas individuales fuertes no siempre se componen bien (mejora esperada del +47% vs. real del +17%). Las ganancias se apilan de forma diferente para recuperación y fidelidad, pudiendo una optimizar la otra. La mejor composición cambia con el tamaño del corpus.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Las mejoras medidas de forma aislada no predicen el rendimiento real al componer técnicas RAG. Es crucial evaluar las nuevas técnicas junto con el resto de la pila para obtener resultados fiables y aplicables en la práctica.

papers.title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance across embodied manipulation tasks by unifying visual understanding, language conditioning, and action generation. However, long-horizon tasks can involve non-Markovian dependencies: successful decisions may require retaining task progress and past interaction outcomes, while partial observability and execution errors compound over time. Existing work has begun to address these challenges by augmenting foundation-model policies with memory and by introducing hierarchical architectures that separate high-level planning from low-level execution. We organize the high-level VLM as a robotic agent through an editable harness to maintain task context and improve planning through execution experience. We instantiate this approach as SERA (Self-Evolving Robotic Agent), with a fixed VLA executor providing low-level control. The harness maintains and updates task context using observations and execution feedback to guide subsequent planning. Self-evolution uses environment rollouts to propose and evaluate harness revisions, with the selected configuration fixed before held-out testing. On RoboMME, SERA achieves 51.38% overall success with autonomous selection, compared with 44.38% without self-evolution. Our exploration suggests that agentic planning is a promising direction for history-dependent robotic manipulation.

summary_es.tldr: Agentes robóticos autoevolutivos mejoran la manipulación en tareas complejas al recordar y aprender de la experiencia pasada.
summary_es.problema: Las tareas robóticas de largo alcance a menudo requieren recordar el progreso y los resultados de interacciones pasadas, algo que los modelos actuales de visión-lenguaje-acción (VLA) tienen dificultades para manejar debido a la dependencia no Markoviana, la observación parcial y los errores de ejecución.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone SERA (Self-Evolving Robotic Agent), un agente robótico que organiza un modelo VLA como un planificador de alto nivel. Utiliza un 'harness' editable para mantener y actualizar el contexto de la tarea basándose en observaciones y retroalimentación de ejecución, y se autoevoluciona mediante la exploración del entorno para proponer y evaluar revisiones del 'harness'.
summary_es.resultados: SERA logra un éxito general del 51.38% en la tarea RoboMME con selección autónoma, superando el 44.38% obtenido sin el mecanismo de autoevolución.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Demuestra que la planificación agentiva, que permite a los robots aprender y adaptarse a partir de su historial de interacciones, es una dirección prometedora para mejorar la manipulación robótica en escenarios complejos y dependientes del historial.

papers.title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Agent harnesses have become a central component of modern agentic systems, shaping how models use tools, manage context, and coordinate long-horizon interaction. Realizing the benefits of these harnesses depends on how effectively the underlying model can make use of them, motivating reinforcement learning directly through the harness. However, existing approaches typically train through a single fixed harness, which can lead to specialization and limited transfer across harness configurations. To address this, we introduce \textbf{Harness Scaling}, a new scaling dimension for agentic RL that extends training from a single harness to diverse execution configurations. Concretely, we construct a factorized harness space, select a compact training subset with balanced factorial coverage, and organize cross-harness training to combine global coverage with controlled variation for the same task. Across multiple benchmarks, model scales, and RL algorithms, Harness Scaling consistently improves generalization to unseen white-box configurations. Moreover, models trained through structured white-box variation transfer effectively to unseen external black-box harnesses, outperforming models trained through a single complex black-box harness. These results establish harness diversity as a meaningful scaling dimension for agentic RL and highlight the importance of how this diversity is organized for cross-harness generalization.

summary_es.tldr: Entrena agentes de IA con diversas configuraciones de 'harness' para mejorar su adaptabilidad y generalización a tareas nuevas.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes de IA entrenados con una única configuración de 'harness' (herramienta de interacción) se especializan demasiado y no se transfieren bien a otras configuraciones.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce 'Harness Scaling', un método que entrena agentes a través de un conjunto diverso y estructurado de configuraciones de 'harness', en lugar de una sola.
summary_es.resultados: Los modelos entrenados con 'Harness Scaling' muestran una mejor generalización a configuraciones de 'harness' no vistas (white-box) y también a 'harnesses' externos (black-box), superando a los métodos tradicionales.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Mejora la robustez y adaptabilidad de los agentes de IA, permitiéndoles funcionar eficazmente en entornos y con herramientas de interacción variadas sin reentrenamiento extensivo.

papers.title: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
papers.abstract_en: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers. To escape local minima in the discovery, we propose to encourage orthogonal exploration by constructing the team using agents with varying expertise. However, realizing this design requires more than diverse backgrounds. When experiments are costly, a team can test only a limited number of ideas, thereby creating the need to balance exploration and exploitation when selecting a subset of researchers to propose and execute new experiments. Furthermore, each result should shape what the team tries next. We therefore ask how AI researchers with different scientific backgrounds can build on one another's findings and sustain progress under a limited experimental budget. To address these challenges, we build a team of persistent AI researchers, each grounded in a different discipline, who keep private research histories, share experimental evidence, and receive research opportunities through adaptive allocation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this design by deploying the team to search for linear attention architectures, where it outperforms GDN2 at 1.3B scale on language modeling, common-sense reasoning, and synthetic and real-world retrieval tasks. In controlled comparisons, removing any single organizational component from our design yields markedly weaker discoveries: without disciplinary backgrounds, the search plateaus early; without private histories, researchers make less progress despite identical shared evidence; and uniform selection falls short of adaptive allocation within the same budget. These results suggest that sustained autonomous discovery depends not only on stronger agents, but also on who explores, what they remember, and how research effort is allocated.

summary_es.tldr: Equipos de IA colaborativos descubren arquitecturas de atención lineal más rápido y mejor que los métodos existentes.
summary_es.problema: Acelerar el descubrimiento científico con IA requiere superar la exploración limitada y la necesidad de que los agentes construyan sobre los hallazgos de otros, especialmente con presupuestos experimentales limitados.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone un equipo de investigadores de IA persistentes, cada uno con una disciplina diferente, que mantienen historiales de investigación privados, comparten evidencia experimental y reciben oportunidades de investigación a través de asignación adaptativa.
summary_es.resultados: El equipo propuesto supera a GDN2 a escala de 1.3B en modelado de lenguaje, razonamiento de sentido común y tareas de recuperación. Eliminar componentes clave del diseño (antecedentes disciplinarios, historiales privados, asignación adaptativa) debilita significativamente los descubrimientos.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Demuestra que la organización y la asignación de recursos de los equipos de IA son cruciales para el descubrimiento autónomo sostenido, no solo la potencia individual de los agentes.

papers.title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
papers.abstract_en: Cooperative language-model agents can improve without weight updates by revising reusable skills, but only if a shared team reward is traced to the responsible agent and skill. Existing methods credit the skills present in each trajectory, yet presence is not responsibility: a harmful skill active in successful runs still earns positive credit. We present \textbf{GRSE}, \textbf{G}roup-\textbf{R}elative \textbf{S}kill \textbf{E}volution, which assigns behavioral credit by comparison: inspired by GRPO, it executes each question several times under the same skill libraries and contrasts the executions to credit agent--skill pairs, with structured diagnosis of failures. On HotpotQA and LoCoMo with two open-weight actors, GRSE outperforms MASkills, the closest prior method, on HotpotQA and every LoCoMo category except open-domain, with the largest gains on multi-hop questions ($+6.7$ and $+3.2$ F1). Its gains rest on better-grounded retrieval rather than answers given without evidence, and its learned skills transfer between the multi-hop tasks. GRSE is robust to corrupted libraries: starting from planted harmful skills, it credits every planted skill with the correct sign and recovers the score of a clean library ($+6.3$ points), whereas MASkills misattributes two and falls below its starting point.

summary_es.tldr: Mejora la colaboración de agentes de IA sin reentrenamiento, identificando qué habilidades de equipo son realmente responsables del éxito o fracaso.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes de IA colaborativos que mejoran sin actualizar sus pesos (revisando habilidades reutilizables) tienen dificultades para asignar correctamente el crédito de la recompensa compartida a los agentes y habilidades específicos que contribuyeron al resultado, lo que lleva a la asignación de crédito positivo a habilidades perjudiciales.
summary_es.propuesta: Se presenta GRSE (Group-Relative Skill Evolution), un método que asigna crédito conductual mediante comparación. Ejecuta cada pregunta varias veces con las mismas bibliotecas de habilidades y contrasta las ejecuciones para asignar crédito a pares de agentes-habilidades, incluyendo un diagnóstico estructurado de fallos.
summary_es.resultados: GRSE supera a MASkills en HotpotQA y en la mayoría de categorías de LoCoMo, con mejoras significativas en preguntas de múltiples saltos (+6.7 y +3.2 F1). Recupera el rendimiento de bibliotecas corruptas (+6.3 puntos), a diferencia de MASkills que falla en la atribución.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite la mejora continua y segura de equipos de agentes de IA sin costosos reentrenamientos, asegurando que las habilidades que perjudican al equipo sean identificadas y corregidas, lo que es crucial para aplicaciones prácticas y robustas.
